summary: Device-trust MFA assertion failures on macOS block Console login for managed devices
description: Summary: Several engineers reported being unable to complete SSO into Redwood Console from company-managed macOS devices. The SSO flow stalls at device-trust / platform authenticator step showing a generic 'Unable to verify device' message. Impact: blocked access to Console for ~14 employees in us-east; affects internal ops and oncall rotations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a company-managed macOS (Ventura+), open Console URL behind SSO
2) Primary Okta SSO redirect completes, prompted for device verification (Touch ID/Face ID dialog appears)
3) After approving on-device prompt, browser shows 'Device verification failed' and login does not complete
4) Attempting to use fallback OTP returns success but device trust remains unverified for future logins
observed_logs: Browser console (Chrome): WebAuthn: "signature verification failed" from relying party check
Okta system log (event id okta-logs-20260312-07): 'webauthn.assertion.verify.failed - signature verification error'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent change in IdP signing keys or JWK cache TTL leading to signature verification mismatch.
Performed repro with test account: observed Okta returns assertion validation error while macOS returns successful user presence. This suggests validation failure on server side.
Checked Okta change log: automated key rotation completed at 2026-03-12T06:50Z (internal note: rotation job id 'rot-20260312-01').
Our device-trust service caches Okta JWKs for 24h; cache refresh job did not pick up new key due to a transient 502 from Okta's jwks endpoint during rotation window.
Private control plane (redwood-private-auth) was using cached JWK set containing old attestation key which no longer verifies assertions signed with the rotated key.
Re-enrolling device (clearing platform credential) produces a new credential signed with current key; newly enrolled credentials validate successfully.
Affected population appears to be devices that had last re-enrolled before 2026-03-12 06:50Z and have not re-authenticated since rotation.
impact_summary: Number of affected users: ~14 engineers (reported via #internal-support and survey)
Services impacted: Redwood Console admin flows, role escalations, oncall runbook access for affected users
Duration: began ~2026-03-12T07:00Z, continuing until workaround applied
workarounds: Short term: Use alternate OTP MFA (email/SMS) or SSO fallback to finish login and then re-enroll device from Console > Security > Device Trust.
Support must trigger remote re-enrollment for users who cannot reach Console by creating a temporary session via SRE support token (documented in Confluence runbook 'device-trust-ops').
Manual fix on server: flush device-trust JWK cache to force fetch of rotated keys (performed as temporary mitigation).
action_items: 1) Roll out immediate cache flush to all control plane replicas and verify JWK fetch success (done 2026-03-12T09:15Z on prod-us-east).
2) Add retry/backoff when fetching jwks to avoid permanent stale cache if endpoint returns transient 5xx.
3) Lower cache TTL from 24h to 5m for JWKs and implement a health check alert if jwks.fetch fails > 3 times in 10m.
4) Update post-rotation runbook to include coordinated cache flush across private/hosted control planes and MDM notifications for re-enrollment window.
5) Outreach: notify internal Slack #internal-support and affected employees with steps to re-enroll and temporary OTP fallback.
6) Follow-up ticket to audit other services that cache IdP jwks (linked issue INT-20671).
resolution: Temporary mitigation: Flushed JWK cache on all prod-us-east replicas (2026-03-12T09:15Z) and confirmed that subsequent assertions validate. Short-term communication sent to affected users with re-enrollment steps. Long-term fix: config and runbook changes scheduled (PR opened).
